### Data Analysis for the Iris Dataset

```{r}
library('tidyverse')
```

Loading the dataset

```{r}
data('iris')
print(iris)
```

Understanding the features our dataset has

```{r}
names(iris)

```

Getting a glimpse of our data to get to understand the structure of our dataset

```{r}
glimpse(iris)
```

A brief summary for the dataset

```{r}
summary(iris)
```

From the data the species are evently selected.

Displaying the null values

```{r}
iris %>% 
  filter(!complete.cases(.)) %>% 
  print()
```

There are no missing values in our dataset hence we can use the data for modelling

### Data Analysis

Displaying relationships between the variables

```{r}
iris %>% 
  select(-Species) %>% 
  cor()
```

There is a strong positive relationship between petal length and petal width also a positive strong relationship between Petal Length, Petal Width with Sepal Length. Also there is a relative weak negative relationship between Sepal Width and Petal Length.

### Data Visualization for the strongest relationship

```{r}
ggplot(iris,aes(x=Petal.Width,y= Petal.Length,color = Species))+
  geom_point(alpha = 0.4)+
  theme_bw()+
  labs(title= "Relationship between Petal Width aganist Petal Length")
  
```

### PLotting a violin plot to understand the distribution of our data

```{r}
ggplot(iris,aes(y = Sepal.Length))+
  geom_violin(trim = FALSE)+
  geom_boxplot(width = 0.5)+
  labs(title = "Violin Chart for the Sepal Length variable")+
  theme_bw()
```

```{r}

ggplot(iris, aes(y = Sepal.Length)) +
  geom_violin(trim = FALSE, fill = "lightblue", color = "darkblue", alpha = 0.5) +  # Added trim, fill, color, and alpha
  geom_boxplot(width = 0.2, fill = "gray", color = "black", alpha = 0.5) +       # Adjusted width, fill, color, and alpha
  labs(title = "Violin and Box Plot of Sepal Length",
       y = "Sepal Length (cm)") +                                    # Improved title and y-axis label
  theme_bw() +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5))  # Centered title
```

Density plot for the Sepal Width

```{r}
ggplot(iris,aes(x = Sepal.Width))+
         geom_density(fill = "skyblue",color = "darkblue",alpha = 0.5)+
         theme_bw()+
         labs(title = "Density plot for the Sepal Width varaible")
        
```

What about the histogram

```{r}
ggplot(iris,aes(x = Sepal.Width))+
  geom_histogram(fill = "skyblue",bins = 10,color = "darkblue")+
  theme_bw()+
  labs(title = "Histogram for the Sepal Width variable",x = "Sepal Width", y = "Frequency")
```

From this it shows that the sepal Width Column is normally distributed with bins = 10

### Boxplots

```{r}
ggplot(iris,aes(x = Sepal.Length))+
  geom_boxplot(width = 0.8 , fill = "maroon",color= "red")+
  theme_bw()+
  labs(title = "Boxplot for the Sepal Length variable",x = "Sepal Length" )
```

From the boxplot we can see that the median is around 5.8 we could try to prove this using the percentiles command

```{r}
q1 = quantile(iris$Sepal.Length,.25)
q2 = quantile(iris$Sepal.Length,.75)
q3 = q2-q1
q3
```

What about using the 50th percentile

```{r}
q3 = quantile(iris$Sepal.Length,.5)
q3
```

Plotting a bar graph for Petal Length aganist species

```{r}
petal_length_summ <- iris %>% 
  select(Petal.Length,Species) %>% 
  group_by(Species) %>% 
  summarise(mean_petal_length = mean(Petal.Length)) %>% 
  print()
```

Now plotting this data in a graph

```{r}
ggplot(petal_length_summ,aes(x = Species , y = mean_petal_length , fill = Species))+
  geom_bar(stat = "identity")+
  theme_bw()+
  labs(title = " Mean Petal Length for each species" , x = "Species" , y = "Mean Petal Length")
```
